quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Residents are reminded that bulky items such as mattresses and old sofas will not be collected with normal rubbish. To arrange a special pickup, call the council at least three days in advance. There is a small charge, which is added to the next council tax bill. Items left outside without a booking may be removed and could lead to a fine.
quests.question: What should someone do to get rid of an old sofa?
options: Book a special collection ahead of time
Leave it out with the normal rubbish
Pay the charge at the council office
Wait for the next tax bill
quests.correctAnswer: Book a special collection ahead of time
quests.hint: The question never uses the word "pickup". Ask which option carries the same meaning.
quests.explanation: "Arrange a special pickup" and "book a special collection" say the same thing. The wrong options reuse words from the passage but describe actions the notice rules out or mentions only as a payment method.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The club's junior section welcomes children aged six to twelve. Sessions are held in the school gym on Saturday mornings, and coaches stress enjoyment over winning. Parents who wish to stay may watch from the balcony, but they are asked not to shout instructions. New families can join a free trial session at any time.
quests.question: What are parents asked to avoid?
options: Staying at the gym
Telling their children what to do during play
Enjoying the game
Watching the session from the balcony above
quests.correctAnswer: Telling their children what to do during play
quests.hint: Separate what parents may do from what they are asked not to do.
quests.explanation: "Not to shout instructions" is restated as not telling children what to do. Watching and staying are explicitly allowed, which is why they attract readers who match words without checking the meaning.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: The children's museum has a new room where visitors can build bridges from wooden blocks and test them with toy cars. Staff members are on hand to answer questions, and the room is intended for children between four and ten. Adults must accompany anyone under seven. The room is open from ten o'clock until four, every day except Monday.
quests.question: Who needs a grown-up with them in the new room?
options: Children younger than seven
Children aged four to ten
Anyone testing a toy car
The staff members
quests.correctAnswer: Children younger than seven
quests.hint: Keep the general age range and the stricter rule apart.
quests.explanation: "Under seven" is paraphrased as "younger than seven." The four-to-ten range describes who the room is for, not who needs supervision.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Members who plan to be away for more than a month can freeze their membership instead of cancelling it. The freeze costs five dollars a month, and the full fee resumes automatically when the member returns. A doctor's note or proof of travel must be shown at the desk. Freezes can be arranged for up to six months at a time.
quests.question: What must a member show in order to freeze the membership?
options: A signed cancellation form
Evidence of the reason for being away
Their membership card
A receipt showing the five dollar payment
quests.correctAnswer: Evidence of the reason for being away
quests.hint: The passage names two documents. Think of one word that covers both.
quests.explanation: A doctor's note and proof of travel are both types of evidence. Recognising a general word for a pair of specific things is a key paraphrase skill.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Guests staying in our garden rooms are invited to enjoy a light breakfast on the veranda, weather permitting. In case of rain, the same breakfast is brought to the lounge. Guests who prefer a hot meal can order cooked dishes from the kitchen for a small extra charge. Vegetarian and gluten-free options are always available.
quests.question: Where will breakfast be served if it is raining?
options: In the garden rooms
In the kitchen
On the veranda
Indoors, in the lounge
quests.correctAnswer: Indoors, in the lounge
quests.hint: Decide what the phrase about weather really means for the plan.
quests.explanation: "In case of rain" tells you the veranda is not used, and the lounge is an indoor space. The kitchen is only where cooked dishes come from.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear Ms. Reyes, thank you for your interest in the design position. After careful consideration, we have decided to offer the role to a candidate with more experience in packaging. We were impressed by your portfolio and will keep your details on file for future openings. Please do not reply to this message.
quests.question: What does the company plan to do with Ms. Reyes's information?
options: Delete it immediately
Send it to a packaging firm
Share it with the successful candidate
Store it in case another job becomes available
quests.correctAnswer: Store it in case another job becomes available
quests.hint: The last sentence contains a set phrase that means something simple.
quests.explanation: "Keep your details on file for future openings" means the company will store her information for other jobs. The rest of the email delivers the bad news politely.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Passengers may bring one small bag into the cabin, provided it fits under the seat in front. Larger cases must go in the hold and are charged by weight. Those who exceed the limit at the gate will pay a higher fee than at the check-in desk. Sports equipment and musical instruments are treated as hold baggage.
quests.question: When is it cheaper to pay for extra weight?
options: At the desk beside the departure gate
Inside the cabin
Before reaching the departure gate
Under the seat
quests.correctAnswer: Before reaching the departure gate
quests.hint: The two places where you can pay appear in one sentence. Compare their prices.
quests.explanation: The gate fee is higher, so the check-in desk is cheaper. Since check-in comes before the gate, the answer is a paraphrase of "before reaching the gate."

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Riverside Adventure Camp runs for five weeks in July and August. Each week has a different theme, such as sailing, robotics or wildlife. Families can register for a single week or the whole summer, and siblings receive a discount on the second place. Lunch and snacks are included in the weekly price.
quests.question: How can a family pay less?
options: By signing up for all five weeks of camp
By choosing the sailing week in July
By registering for a week in August
By enrolling a brother or sister as well
quests.correctAnswer: By enrolling a brother or sister as well
quests.hint: The word "siblings" is not used in any option. What does it mean?
quests.explanation: Siblings are brothers and sisters, and the discount applies to the second place. Nothing in the text says that longer stays or particular themes cost less.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Home delivery slots must be booked at least twenty-four hours ahead and are available from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Orders over sixty dollars are delivered free, while smaller orders carry a four-dollar charge. Frozen items are packed in insulated bags that keep them cold for up to three hours.
quests.question: What happens to orders below sixty dollars?
options: They are packed in insulated bags
They cannot be delivered
They arrive within three hours
A small delivery fee is added
quests.correctAnswer: A small delivery fee is added
quests.hint: In this text, "carry a charge" is not about lifting anything.
quests.explanation: "Carry a four-dollar charge" means a fee is added. The insulated bags apply to frozen items, and three hours is how long they stay cold.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Parking at the hospital costs six dollars a day. Patients who come for regular treatment can ask at the information desk for a monthly permit, which works out considerably cheaper than paying daily. Permits are valid only in Lot 3, and drivers must display them on the windscreen. The information desk is open from eight until six on weekdays.
quests.question: How can patients who come every week keep parking costs down?
options: By paying six dollars per visit
By parking on the street
By obtaining a monthly permit
By showing a receipt on the windscreen
quests.correctAnswer: By obtaining a monthly permit
quests.hint: Find the option that offers a saving, not just a way to pay.
quests.explanation: The permit is the cheaper alternative for regular patients. Paying daily is the standard rate, which the passage says costs more in the long run.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: During May, the library is forgiving all overdue fines. Anyone who returns a late book will not be charged, no matter how long it has been missing. The amnesty aims to bring back books that people are too embarrassed to return. There is a box at the entrance for people who prefer not to speak to anyone.
quests.question: Why is the library cancelling fines this month?
options: To close the library in May
To raise enough money to buy new books
To encourage the return of long-lost books
To punish people who are late
quests.correctAnswer: To encourage the return of long-lost books
quests.hint: The reason follows the verb "aims".
quests.explanation: The amnesty aims to bring back books people are embarrassed about, so the purpose is encouraging returns. "Forgiving fines" is the opposite of punishing.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: At our company, employees choose when to start work, as long as they are present from ten to three. Some come at seven and leave early to collect their children; others begin later and stay into the evening. Managers say output has improved since the policy began. The company has about sixty employees, and most of them work in the city centre.
quests.question: What is required of all employees?
options: Collecting their children
Being at work in the middle of the day
Working late into the evening hours
Starting work at seven in the morning
quests.correctAnswer: Being at work in the middle of the day
quests.hint: Look for the one condition that is the same for everyone.
quests.explanation: Ten to three is the core period everyone must attend, which is the middle of the day. Early starts and late finishes are examples of what is allowed.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Councillors voted on Tuesday to close the old car park behind the market and turn it into a public square. The decision, which passed by seven votes to four, followed a petition signed by more than two thousand residents. Building work is expected to begin next spring. Market traders welcomed the news, although some drivers were unhappy.
quests.question: How was the plan approved?
options: The petition was rejected
A majority of councillors supported it
Every single councillor voted for the plan
It was postponed until spring
quests.correctAnswer: A majority of councillors supported it
quests.hint: Work out what "seven votes to four" says about agreement.
quests.explanation: Seven is more than four, so a majority backed it, but not everyone. Spring refers to when building work starts, not to the approval.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Marek's Bakery has raised the price of its sourdough loaf by fifty cents, its first increase in three years. The owner says flour and energy costs have gone up sharply. He has kept the price of rolls and croissants the same because, he says, they are what most customers buy every morning.
quests.question: Why did the owner leave some prices unchanged?
options: They are his customers' regular purchases
The bakery lost many customers recently
Flour became cheaper
Rolls and croissants cost less to make
quests.correctAnswer: They are his customers' regular purchases
quests.hint: Compare the sourdough with the items that stayed the same, and read the owner's reason.
quests.explanation: The rolls and croissants are what most customers buy daily, which the answer rephrases as regular purchases. The passage does not compare making costs.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The new tram line linking the airport to the city centre will open in early October. The journey will take twenty-two minutes, compared with about forty by bus. Tickets will be sold at stops and through a phone app, and services will run every ten minutes during the day. A single journey will cost three dollars.
quests.question: How does the tram journey compare with the bus?
options: It takes about forty minutes
It runs only in the evening
It takes roughly half as long
It costs twenty-two dollars
quests.correctAnswer: It takes roughly half as long
quests.hint: Turn the two journey times into a simple comparison before looking at the options.
quests.explanation: Twenty-two is close to half of forty. Both numbers appear in wrong options, but each is attached to the wrong thing.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Before you start assembling the shelf, lay out all the parts on the floor and check them against the list in the manual. Fasten the screws loosely at first; tighten them only after all the panels are in place. This makes it easier to line up the holes. If you are working alone, lean the shelf against a wall while you fasten it.
quests.question: Why should the screws be tightened last?
options: So the floor is not scratched
So the parts do not get lost
So the pieces can still be adjusted
So the manual can be checked
quests.correctAnswer: So the pieces can still be adjusted
quests.hint: The last sentence gives the reason in plain words. Paraphrase it in your head.
quests.explanation: Lining up holes needs some movement, which is what loose screws allow. The idea of adjusting is expressed differently in the text.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: To clean the coffee machine, first switch it off and let it cool. Empty the drip tray and rinse it under warm water. Descaling should be done every three months, using the special tablets sold with the machine; ordinary vinegar can damage the internal pipes. Always unplug the machine before cleaning the outside.
quests.question: What should NOT be used to descale the machine?
options: Household vinegar
Warm water
The drip tray
The special tablets
quests.correctAnswer: Household vinegar
quests.hint: Watch for the sentence that contains a warning after a semicolon.
quests.explanation: The warning is about ordinary vinegar, which is the same as household vinegar. The other options are things the text recommends or uses.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: If you cannot log in to your email, do not keep guessing your password, because repeated wrong attempts can lock your account. Use the "forgot password" link instead. A code will be sent to your phone, and you can then create a new password within a few minutes.
quests.question: What is the risk of trying different passwords again and again?
options: The account may be blocked
A code is sent by post
The email is lost forever
The phone number is deleted
quests.correctAnswer: The account may be blocked
quests.hint: Find the cause-and-effect link and rephrase the effect.
quests.explanation: "Lock your account" means the account becomes blocked. The passage does not say anything is deleted or lost forever.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Water restrictions begin on Monday after the driest spring in thirty years. Households may water gardens only in the evening, and washing cars with a hose is banned. Fines start at eighty dollars. Officials say the rules will stay until the reservoirs are back to sixty percent. Parks and sports grounds will also stop watering their grass.
quests.question: How long will the restrictions last?
options: Until the Monday morning
For as long as the summer lasts
Until water storage levels recover
For sixty days after the start
quests.correctAnswer: Until water storage levels recover
quests.hint: The answer describes a condition, not a length of time.
quests.explanation: The rules end when reservoirs are back to sixty percent, so they depend on recovery. "Thirty years" and "sixty" appear in the passage but answer other questions.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Rooftop hives are appearing on office buildings in several large cities. The bees feed on flowers in parks and window boxes, and the honey is sold to local shops. Beekeepers point out that urban bees often do better than country bees, since city gardens bloom for more of the year.
quests.question: Why might city bees do better than country bees?
options: City honey sells for more
Flowers are available for longer
There are fewer beekeepers
Office workers feed them
quests.correctAnswer: Flowers are available for longer
quests.hint: A small word introduces the explanation, and its subject is gardens.
quests.explanation: Gardens that "bloom for more of the year" means flowers are available for longer. The honey sales are a separate point.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: When heavy snow is forecast, the city clears main roads first, then bus routes, then residential streets. Residents on side streets may wait a day or more, so they are advised to keep a supply of food and medicine at home. Pavements outside homes are the responsibility of the owners.
quests.question: Who clears the pavement outside a house?
options: Neighbours on side streets
City workers
The people who own the property
Bus drivers
quests.correctAnswer: The people who own the property
quests.hint: The passage assigns jobs to different groups. Match this job to its group.
quests.explanation: "Responsibility of the owners" is paraphrased as the people who own the property. City crews work on roads, not on pavements.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Students who fail a module in June may resit the exam in August without paying a fee. A second failure means the module must be repeated the following year. Those who miss the August exam for medical reasons must send a doctor's letter within a week. Students should check the exam timetable on the university website.
quests.question: What happens to a student who fails the August resit?
options: They have to take the module again next year
They resit the exam in June
They pay a fee and try the exam once more
They send a doctor's letter within a week
quests.correctAnswer: They have to take the module again next year
quests.hint: The phrase "second failure" refers to a specific attempt. Which one?
quests.explanation: A second failure means failing in August, and the consequence is repeating the module the following year. The fee and the letter belong to other situations.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Your student card is your library pass, your bus ticket and your proof of age. If it is lost, report it at once to the office so the card can be cancelled. A replacement costs ten dollars and takes three working days. Until then, staff can issue a temporary card for the library only.
quests.question: What is the first thing to do after losing the card?
options: Pay ten dollars immediately
Ask the bus company for a temporary pass
Tell the office so it can be blocked
Wait three working days
quests.correctAnswer: Tell the office so it can be blocked
quests.hint: "First" points you to the earliest step, and one phrase means "immediately."
quests.explanation: "Report it at once" is the first action, and "cancelled" is rephrased as blocked. The payment and the waiting come afterwards.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The Hartley Scholarship supports students from families with low incomes who show strong results at school. Winners receive help with tuition for three years, provided they keep their grades up. Applications must include two references and a short essay about the applicant's goals. Decisions are announced in the first week of May.
quests.question: What must winners do to keep receiving support?
options: Find two new references
Apply for a larger scholarship each year
Write a new essay each year
Continue to perform well academically
quests.correctAnswer: Continue to perform well academically
quests.hint: A conditional word introduces the requirement for the later years.
quests.explanation: "Provided they keep their grades up" means keep performing well. The essay and references are for the application stage only.

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Phone batteries last longer if they are not left at full charge for days at a time. Many experts advise keeping the level between twenty and eighty percent and avoiding leaving the phone in a hot car. Heat, more than anything else, shortens a battery's life. Fast charging is convenient, but it also produces more warmth.
quests.question: What harms a battery most?
options: Charging from twenty percent
High temperatures
Switching it off
Using it at night
quests.correctAnswer: High temperatures
quests.hint: The strongest claim in the passage is marked by a comparison.
quests.explanation: "Heat, more than anything else" shows it is the biggest factor, and heat is the same as high temperature. Twenty percent is a recommended lower limit, not a harmful condition.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: A password manager stores all your passwords in one encrypted place, so you only have to remember a single strong one. It can also create long random passwords for each site. The main risk is forgetting the master password, since recovery is often impossible. Some managers are free, while others charge a small yearly fee.
quests.question: What is the biggest danger of using a password manager?
options: Losing the one password that opens everything
Using one password for every site
Storing passwords in an unlocked file
Creating random passwords for every site
quests.correctAnswer: Losing the one password that opens everything
quests.hint: Think about what "master" means, then find the risk in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The master password is the single key to all the others, so forgetting it is the main risk. The other options are ideas the manager is designed to solve.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: During a video call, mute your microphone when you are not speaking, since background noise can distract everyone. If you have a poor connection, turning off your camera can help improve the sound. It is also polite to tell the host beforehand if you need to leave early.
quests.question: How can someone with a weak connection improve the call?
options: Mute their microphone
Switch off their camera
Ask the host to speak louder
Leave the meeting early
quests.correctAnswer: Switch off their camera
quests.hint: Two different tips are given for two different problems. Match the problem first.
quests.explanation: A poor connection is helped by turning off the camera, while muting deals with background noise. Both tips share a sentence-like structure, which invites mixing them up.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Travel insurance usually covers medical costs abroad, lost luggage and cancelled flights, but not everything. Injuries from risky activities such as skiing may be excluded unless you pay extra, and conditions you already had before the trip are often not included. It is worth reading the small print before buying, because the cheapest policy is rarely the most complete.
quests.question: Why does the writer advise reading the small print?
options: Medical costs are never covered abroad
Skiing is always banned on insured trips
Insurance is unnecessary for short trips abroad
Low-priced policies may leave out important protection
quests.correctAnswer: Low-priced policies may leave out important protection
quests.hint: The final clause gives the writer's reason. Work out what "complete" means for a policy.
quests.explanation: A "complete" policy covers more, so a cheap one may leave things out. The examples of skiing and prior conditions show what could be missing.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The community centre offers a wide range of classes, from pottery to computing for beginners. Prices are kept low because the building is run largely by volunteers, and local shops help pay for equipment. Anyone on a low income can ask the manager for a reduced rate on any course.
quests.question: How does the centre keep its prices low?
options: It charges less for pottery than for computing
It teaches only beginners
It is owned by local shops
It relies on unpaid helpers and local support
quests.correctAnswer: It relies on unpaid helpers and local support
quests.hint: The word "because" holds the answer, and it has two parts.
quests.explanation: Volunteers are unpaid helpers, and shops that help pay for equipment are local support. Neither means the shops own the centre.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Shoppers who use the store's loyalty card earn one point for every dollar spent. Two hundred points can be exchanged for a ten-dollar voucher. Points expire after twelve months, so customers who shop only occasionally may lose them before they can be used. Vouchers, however, remain valid for six months.
quests.question: Who is most likely to lose their points?
options: Customers who rarely visit the store
Shoppers already holding vouchers
People who spend a lot of money each week
People who joined last month
quests.correctAnswer: Customers who rarely visit the store
quests.hint: Think about who would take longer than a year to reach the required number.
quests.explanation: Occasional shoppers collect points slowly, so twelve months may pass first. Vouchers last six months and are not affected by the expiry of points.
